subject: ela
intro: This test covers the whole Vocabulary Acquisition and Use cluster across all three standards: determining word meanings with clues and word parts (3.L.C.4), understanding word relationships and figurative language (3.L.C.5), and using grade-level and signal words (3.L.C.6). Each question is multiple choice and labeled with the standard it checks.

items.prompt:
Use the suffix.

The garden was so peaceful that we sat quietly for an hour.

The suffix -ful in "peaceful" means the word means
A) without peace
B) full of peace
C) before peace
D) peace again

steps: The suffix -ful means "full of."
So peaceful means full of peace.
The answer is B.

items.prompt:
Use context clues.

The cave was so dim that we needed a flashlight to see the walls.

What does "dim" most likely mean?
A) very bright
B) not much light, dark
C) very loud
D) very cold

steps: The clue is they "needed a flashlight to see."
That means the cave had little light.
So dim means dark, B.

items.prompt:
Use the prefix.

The magician made the coin disappear from his hand.

What does "disappear" mean?
A) to appear again
B) to go out of sight
C) to shine brightly
D) to appear before
items.answer: B) to go out of sight

steps: The prefix dis- means "not" or "the opposite of."
"Appear" means to come into sight.
So disappear means to go out of sight, B.
solution.answer: B) to go out of sight

items.prompt:
This word has two meanings. Use context clues.

The scientist wrote a note in the margin, then closed the heavy book.

What does "note" mean here?
A) a musical sound
B) a short written message
C) to notice something
D) a piece of money

steps: "Note" can mean a musical sound, a written message, or to notice.
The clue is that she "wrote a note in the margin" of a book.
So here note means a short written message, B.

items.prompt:
What does the underlined phrase mean?

After running the race, Sam was as hungry as a bear.

"As hungry as a bear" means
A) not hungry at all
B) very hungry
C) a little tired
D) very happy

steps: The phrase is figurative.
It compares Sam to a hungry bear.
It means very hungry, so B.

items.prompt:
Which sentence uses figurative language?

A) The boy kicked the soccer ball.
B) The rain fell on the roof.
C) The thunder growled like an angry giant.
D) The teacher read a book to the class.
items.answer: C) The thunder growled like an angry giant.

steps: Figurative language does not mean exactly what it says.
Thunder cannot really growl like a giant.
So the answer is C.
solution.answer: C) The thunder growled like an angry giant.

items.prompt:
Which order goes from the SMALLEST feeling to the biggest?

A) starving, peckish, hungry
B) peckish, hungry, starving
C) hungry, peckish, starving
D) starving, hungry, peckish

steps: All three words are about wanting food.
"Peckish" is only a little hungry.
"Hungry" is more, and "starving" is the most, so B.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence.

The puzzle was a walk in the park, so Lin finished it before lunch.

Which statement is TRUE about "a walk in the park"?
A) It is literal, meaning Lin went to a park
B) It is figurative, meaning the puzzle was very easy
C) It is literal, meaning Lin walked while thinking
D) It is figurative, meaning the puzzle was very hard
items.answer: B) It is figurative, meaning the puzzle was very easy

steps: There is no real park in the sentence, so it is figurative.
The clue is that Lin "finished it before lunch."
"A walk in the park" means very easy, so B.
solution.answer: B) It is figurative, meaning the puzzle was very easy

items.prompt:
Choose the best word.

We read a story ______ we fell asleep.

A) before
B) above
C) beneath
D) beside

steps: The blank needs a time word.
Reading came first, then sleep.
So "before" fits, A.

items.prompt:
Choose the best academic word.

The teacher asked us to ______ the two animals and tell how they are alike.

A) compare
B) sprint
C) sneeze
D) whisper

steps: The clue is telling how two animals are alike.
That is what it means to compare.
So the answer is A.

items.prompt:
Which sentence uses a spatial word correctly?

A) The lamp sits beside the couch.
B) The lamp sits during the couch.
C) We ate lunch above we played.
D) We slept beneath we woke up.
items.answer: A) The lamp sits beside the couch.

steps: A spatial word tells where something is.
"Beside the couch" correctly tells where the lamp is.
The other choices use words wrongly, so A.
solution.answer: A) The lamp sits beside the couch.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence.

______ the storm, the family waited beneath the strong roof until it passed.

Which choice fills the blank AND names the word type correctly?
A) Beside, a temporal word
B) During, a temporal word
C) During, a spatial word
D) Above, a temporal word

steps: The blank tells when the family waited, in the time of the storm.
"During" fits and tells when, so it is a temporal word.
So the answer is B.
